questions.stem: Differentiate \(\left(e^{x} + x\right)^{4}\).
questions.hint: Chain rule: outer power first, then multiply by the derivative of the inside \(e^{x}+x\).

steps.explain: The expression \(\left(e^{x}+x\right)^{4}\) is a composite function: an outer power and an inner sum. Set the inner function equal to \(u\), so the outer function is a pure power of \(u\).
Differentiate the outer power with respect to \(u\): \(\dfrac{dy}{du}=4u^{3}\). (Power rule: bring the 4 down and reduce the index by 1.).
Differentiate the inner function term by term: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}e^{x}=e^{x}\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}x=1\). Add them to get \(u'\).
Apply the chain rule \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy}{du}\cdot\dfrac{du}{dx}\): multiply \(4u^{3}\) by \((e^{x}+1)\).

questions.stem: (a) What is the first time after 9:45 am at which the flow rate is zero?
questions.hint: Set the sine factor equal to zero and take the first positive \(t\).
questions.solution: The correct answer is \(t = 30\) minutes after 9:45 am (10:15 am).

steps.explain:
Flow rate zero means \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0\). Given \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -0.3\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\), and \(-0.3 
eq 0\), we need \(\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{30} = 0\).
Sine is zero when its argument is an integer multiple of \(\pi\): \(\dfrac{\pi t}{30} = n\pi\) for integer \(n\), so \(t = 30n\).
The first time after 9:45 am is the first positive solution: \(n = 1\) gives \(t = 30\) minutes. (\(n = 0\) is the switch-on instant, not “after”.)
Clock time: 9:45 am plus 30 minutes is 10:15 am. A common slip solves \(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30}=0\) (that would be extrema of volume, not zero flow).
Final answer: \(t = 30\) minutes after 9:45 am (10:15 am).

questions.stem: (b) Find an expression for the volume \(V\) of water in the pool after \(t\) minutes.
questions.hint: Integrate \(dV/dt\) and use \(V(0)=100\).

steps.explain: Volume is the integral of flow rate: \(V(t) = \int -0.3\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\,dt\). Why integrate? Flow rate is \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}\), so volume is an antiderivative of the given rate.
Chain rule reverse: let \(u = \dfrac{\pi t}{30}\), then \(du = \dfrac{\pi}{30}\,dt\). \(\int\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\,dt = -\dfrac{30}{\pi}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\).
Therefore \(\int -0.3\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\,dt = -0.3\left(-\dfrac{30}{\pi}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\right) + C = \dfrac{9}{\pi}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} + C\) (since \(0.3\times 30 = 9\)).
Initial condition: pool full at \(t = 0\), so \(V(0) = 100\). Then \(100 = \dfrac{9}{\pi}\cos 0 + C = \dfrac{9}{\pi} + C\), hence \(C = 100 - \dfrac{9}{\pi}\).
Combine: \(V(t) = \dfrac{9}{\pi}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} + 100 - \dfrac{9}{\pi} = 100 + \dfrac{9}{\pi}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} - 1\right)\).
Final answer: \(V = 100 + \dfrac{9}{\pi}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} - 1\right)\). Check: at \(t=0\), cos = 1 so \(V=100\). A common slip flips the sign in front of the cosine term.

questions.stem: (c) Find the minimum volume of water in the pool during the pumping cycle. Leave your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
questions.hint: Minimise the cosine term in the expression from (b).

steps.explain: From part (b): \(V(t) = 100 + \dfrac{9}{\pi}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} - 1\right)\). The constant 100 and \(-\dfrac{9}{\pi}\) do not change which cos value minimises \(V\).
Since \(\dfrac{9}{\pi} > 0\), \(V\) is minimised when \(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30}\) is minimised. The minimum of cosine is \(-1\).
When does this occur? \(\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{30} = -1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\pi t}{30} = \pi \Rightarrow t = 30\) min (same instant as zero flow in part (a) for the first cycle trough).
Final answer: \(V_{\min} = 100 - \dfrac{18}{\pi}\) kL. A common slip uses \(\cos = 0\) or forgets the \(-1\) inside the brackets and gets \(100 - \dfrac{9}{\pi}\).
